correctness.rationale: Over the algebraic closure, the trivial idempotent gives dual numbers and each nontrivial unordered inverse-character pair gives a full 2 by 2 block. Odd order excludes other fixed characters. Frobenius permutes these blocks, with center of the descended simple algebra equal to F_(q^d) on a length-d orbit; finite fields split the central simple algebra. In each matrix block, a nonzero square-zero matrix has image equal to kernel, a line. Its commuting square-zero matrices are its scalar multiples by the centralizer calculation. Conversely, for two nonzero square-zero matrices, even one-sided zero product forces equality of those lines, hence both products vanish. Left multiplication acts on two columns and has k-rank 2d; the dual-number contribution is rank 1 for each nonzero scalar. Counting a unique line per nonzero tuple yields the full polynomial and all-zero normalizations. Enlarging a compatible space to the product of its projections proves maximality is blockwise, and the linear span of E-1 gives the elementary abelian correspondence. Over the closure the local reduced locus is the cone over P^1 times P^(r-1) in bidegree (2,1): the line [u:v] gives nilpotent direction [uv:u^2:v^2:uv]. Its product with the other blocks and the affine dual-number locus yields the claimed irreducibility and dimension, not original-scheme reducedness. Direct independent enumeration confirmed the 512 individual elements in each order-nine example and the distinct 22,720 and 40,000 ordered pair totals; the maximal-space counts 27 and 81 follow from Frobenius orbit degrees (1,3) versus (1,1,1,1), not from brute-force subspace enumeration.

The bounded enumeration does not independently count maximal subspaces or prove the unbounded statement.
